description: A false-colour infrared satellite or aerial map showing a fragmented landscape with different land cover types delineated by black-outlined polygons. Dense, healthy vegetation appears in shades of deep red. Areas with sparser vegetation, bare ground, or dry grasslands appear in lighter, desaturated pinks and greys. Numeric 4-digit codes in yellow text label the polygons, indicating specific land cover classes. Prominent labels visible include "4212" (appearing in multiple locations, one of which is highlighted by a yellow arrow), "3110", "4100", and "3410", along with a partially visible "42" at the top edge. The yellow arrow specifically points to a narrow, light-coloured linear feature within a polygon labelled "4212", which otherwise appears as a lighter, desaturated area compared to the surrounding red vegetation. While no legend is present, the image context suggests these codes represent various grassland and semi-natural vegetation types, such as Mediterranean alluvial meadows or wet grasslands. No scale bar, compass, or reference year is visible.
